open_obligations: Note that Bai et al.'s concern is the AI feedback model's decisions, while Kirchner et al. study the policy's solutions.
Check whether legibility to small verifiers transfers to humans beyond grade-school math.
Note the legibility tax relative to correctness-only RL.
in.other_title: Prover-verifier games (checkability training) improve legibility of LLM math solutions
in.rationale: Bai et al. warn that scaling supervision may automate and obscure decision making and rely on chain-of-thought for legibility. Kirchner et al. report that optimising only for answer correctness makes solutions less legible to time-limited humans, and that prover-verifier checkability training restores legibility with a legibility tax; the concern is solution legibility in math, not the legibility of an AI supervisor's decisions.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether training can keep model reasoning legible to overseers rather than obscuring it, for chain-of-thought math solutions
